solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Collapse, exhausted, after onset of flu

indicators.note: the exhausted piece is placed after the first letter, so it follows in the entry
the onset of something is its beginning, so take the opening letter of flu

parts.note: all in is an informal phrase for worn out

explanation.surface: Someone worn out at the start of a bout of influenza simply collapses.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall in is to cave in or give way, as a roof or tunnel does when it collapses.

clue.text: Where strikers may be found seeing game on television?

parts.note: a match is a game or contest
the box is a colloquial name for the television set

explanation.surface: A viewer watches a football game on TV, looking for the strikers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikers' looks like footballers, but here they are matches that strike a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Matches, which strike to light, are kept in a small cardboard container.

clue.text: Pompous official judge's first with spirit to support censure

indicators.note: in a down entry, the pieces below hold up the censure piece, which therefore comes first

parts.note: to pan something is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: the first of judge's is its opening letter

parts.note: and has the sense of together with
rum is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: A self-important official is criticised, with the judge leading and a drink being involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Panjandrum is a mock title, coined by Samuel Foote, for a person who gives themselves airs of great authority.

clue.text: Pack exhibit, needing time for hotel

indicators.note: time goes in place of hotel, the clue's for marking the swap

parts.note: to show something is to exhibit it
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone packs up an exhibition, needing time to get to the hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stow is to pack or store things away neatly.

clue.text: My company has something in the blood that causes pneumonia, perhaps

parts.note: plasma is the fluid part of blood

explanation.surface: A firm owner boasts of a blood product that can cause pneumonia.
explanation.definitionFit: This bacterium is a well-known cause of atypical pneumonia; 'perhaps' admits it causes other illnesses too.

clue.text: Design a thing to catch insect

indicators.note: the run of words Design a thing holds the insect within it, catching it

explanation.surface: An inventor tries to design a device to trap insects.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, a kind of insect.

clue.text: Question skill with unknown mineral

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation
Z is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A geologist questions someone's skill at identifying an unknown mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Quartz is a common crystalline mineral made of silica.

clue.text: First couple of subs quietly sat and thought

indicators.note: the first couple of letters of subs are its opening two

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
to sit for a portrait is to pose, so sat is posed

explanation.surface: A pair of substitutes sat quietly on the bench, thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Supposed means believed or assumed, the past tense of think in that sense.

clue.text: A lady will be upset about male, tense in a determined way

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the male and tense pieces
upset means overturned or jumbled, so the letters of a lady are rearranged

parts.note: a man is a male person
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A woman will be upset by a man who is tense and stubborn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be upset' turns A LADY into ADALY, and 'about' wraps that round MANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamantly means firmly and unyieldingly, refusing to be moved.

clue.text: North American university game and state

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
RU stands for rugby union, the game

explanation.surface: An American college game and state legislature sound like a sports report.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a small island nation in the Pacific, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Infection resulting from Spooner's Scottish legislation?

indicators.note: named after Rev Spooner, who swapped the starting sounds of words, so the opening sounds of the two pieces are exchanged

parts.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman, used here as Scottish
law means legislation

explanation.surface: A clue asks which infection could result from Scots law.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of JOCK LAW gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus, the bacterial infection that stiffens the jaw muscles, is commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Work on criminal court appearance

indicators.note: in an across entry the work piece is placed on, after, the jumbled letters
criminal suggests something wrong or crooked, so the letters of court are rearranged

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A defendant's appearance in criminal court involves some work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' is the anagram signal, and 'on' puts the work after the rearranged letters; 'appearance' is a geological one, not a court date.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock that appears at the surface, an emergence of the bedrock.

clue.text: Essence of writer needing change of heart

indicators.note: the middle letter of the writer piece is swapped for another

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: The core of a writer's work needed a change of heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing change of heart' swaps the I at the centre of NIB for U.
explanation.definitionFit: The nub is the central point or crux of a matter.

clue.text: No voting system accepted by central American country's annual awards

indicators.note: the voting system piece is taken inside the country piece

parts.note: Belize is a country in Central America; with the possessive it gives Belize's
PR is proportional representation, a voting system

explanation.surface: A Central American country turns down a voting system.
explanation.definitionFit: These prizes in sciences, literature and peace are awarded each year in Stockholm and Oslo.

clue.text: Supporting worker in arrears

parts.note: to be behind someone is to support them
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A supportive employee has fallen behind with payments.
explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means late or behind schedule, especially with payments owed.

clue.text: Cash required by needy mayor in trouble

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disorder, so the letters of needy mayor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poor mayor in difficulty needs cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready money is cash at hand, available for immediate payment.

clue.text: Person who will arrange 28 regularly in pine, say

indicators.note: the regular letters go inside the tree piece

parts.note: fir is a conifer, a tree like a pine

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from the answer to 28 across picks every other one

parts.note: the answer to 28 across, a verb meaning do better than

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a meeting in a pine forest, regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters, the second and fourth, of EXCEL, giving XE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixer is someone who arranges things, often by unofficial or underhand means.

clue.text: Looked nervous seeing unusually gifted newspaper leader

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of gifted appear in a different order

parts.note: an ed, editor, leads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A talented newspaper editor appeared nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: To fidget is to make restless movements, a sign of being nervous.

clue.text: Plans ahead, rejecting experiences

indicators.note: to reject is to send back, so the letters are read backwards
the setter gives no separate word for the hidden run; the comma closes off the words plans ahead as the stretch whose letters are taken

explanation.surface: Someone plans ahead, turning down experiences.
explanation.walkthrough: The run SAH sits across planS AHead and 'rejecting' reads it backwards; the hidden step is signalled only by the comma closing off the two words, a loose convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something happen to you is to experience it, as in has a good time.

clue.text: Power resting in a concealed pest

indicators.note: the power piece sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: hid means concealed
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Power lies within a hidden pest.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphids are sap-sucking insects that damage garden plants.

clue.text: Sulphur found in pignut barrel?

indicators.note: the sulphur piece is located inside the other

parts.note: read as pig nut: a hog is a pig, and nut is slang for head
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Sulphur is detected in a pignut, a small edible tuber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pignut' is a real plant, but must be split into pig and nut; the question mark flags the barrel as one particular cask.
explanation.definitionFit: A hogshead is a large cask, a barrel of a specific capacity for wine or beer.

clue.text: Sort of programme producing a comedy turn?

indicators.note: producing suggests making something new out of the letters of a comedy turn, which are rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV producer makes a comedy act.
explanation.definitionFit: A documentary is a factual programme, the opposite of a comedy turn.

clue.text: Secure simple job covering line

indicators.note: the easy-task piece wraps around the line piece

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy to do

explanation.surface: Someone secures an easy job that covers a phone line.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to secure or settle it conclusively.

clue.text: Stick that may be chewed

definitions.meaning: glue, something used to stick things together

explanation.surface: A stick of something chewy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is both an adhesive and a sweet one chews.

clue.text: Guard duties firstly adopted by underground worker

indicators.note: the first letter is taken into the miner piece

parts.note: a miner works underground

indicators.note: firstly points to the opening letter of duties

explanation.surface: A miner takes on a guarding role among his first duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A minder is a bodyguard, someone who protects another person.

clue.text: Inscription from untidy heap covering bed?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are wrapped around the bed piece
untidy means messed up, so the letters of heap are rearranged

parts.note: pit is British slang for bed

explanation.surface: An untidy heap is thrown over a garden bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' rearranges the heap's letters, which then go around the bed; 'bed' is slang for where you sleep, not a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is a short text inscribed on a tomb or memorial.

clue.text: Ancient Scottish notice protecting the centre of Mull

indicators.note: the notice piece goes around the central letters, guarding them

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a public notice

indicators.note: the centre of Mull is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: An ancient Scottish notice guards the middle of Mull, a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Auld is the Scots word for old, as in Auld Lang Syne.

clue.text: Low layer attached to end of altar rail

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

indicators.note: the end of altar is its last letter

parts.note: a hen is a layer of eggs

explanation.surface: A low-lying layer is attached to the end of an altar rail in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like part of the altar rail, but it is the bird family.
explanation.definitionFit: The moorhen is a water bird belonging to the rail family.

clue.text: Sailor offering check on board

definitions.meaning: a ship's officer below the captain, as in first officer
the winning move in chess when the king cannot escape

explanation.surface: A sailor offers to check things on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests a ship, but it is the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a ship's officer and checkmate.

clue.text: Do better than 40 in Latin oral

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the numeral is said as two letters

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone outdoes a forty-year-old in a Latin oral exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outshine or surpass others.

clue.text: Remote and strange view of Paris

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd, so the letters of remote and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remote and unusual view of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame cathedral is one of the famous sights of Paris.
